- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.67) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 10–20% for 2–3 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — if forecast is far from recent history (e.g., >0.5 stddev), adjust toward historical mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67); use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7–14 day mean to anchor forecast.  
- Overshoots in high-sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment >0.8) are common; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 7-day high to avoid runaway inflation.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >0.3 in 3 consecutive days, model is likely underestimating volatility — increase forecast by 0.1–0.2 per day until convergence.
